legend: Given two integers n%%ZSMJ0%% and k%%ZSMJ1%%. An array a%%ZSMJ2%% is considered good if the following conditions hold:
The length of a%%ZSMJ3%% is equal to n%%ZSMJ4%%.
The sum of elements of a%%ZSMJ6%% is equal to k%%ZSMJ7%% (i.e. ∑ai=k%%ZSMJ8%%).

The cost of the array a%%ZSMJ9%% is equal to the sum of ai%%ZSMJ10%% &%%ZSMJ11%% ai−1%%ZSMJ12%% for all i%%ZSMJ13%% such that 1<i≤n%%ZSMJ14%%, where &%%ZSMJ15%% is the bitwise AND[9]%%ZSMJ16%% operator.
Your task is to find the minimum cost of a good array.
input: The first line of the input contains a single integer t%%ZSMJ17%% (1≤t≤5000%%ZSMJ18%%) — the number of test cases.
Each line of the following t%%ZSMJ19%% lines of the input consists of two space-separated integers n%%ZSMJ20%% and k%%ZSMJ21%% (1≤n≤106,n≤k≤109%%ZSMJ22%%).
Notice that there is no limit on the sum of n%%ZSMJ23%% over all the test cases.
output: Output t%%ZSMJ24%% lines, the i%%ZSMJ25%%-th of which contains a single integer — the minimum cost of a good array in the i%%ZSMJ26%%-th testcase.
